meaning: Goes to the incinerator. Food scraps, paper that can't be recycled, clothes, rubber, leather, and any plastic that is dirty or mixed with other materials.
elsewhere: 可燃ごみ (kanen), 燃えるごみ (moeru)

meaning: Goes to landfill. Metal, ceramics, non-drink glass, small appliances, umbrellas, foil. Twice a month only.
elsewhere: 不燃ごみ (funen), 燃えないごみ (moenai), 金属・陶器・ガラスごみ

meaning: Paper (newspaper, magazines, cardboard, cartons, other paper), drink bottles, cans and PET bottle bodies. Each goes in its own bundle, box or net.
elsewhere: 資源物 (shigenbutsu), びん・かん・ペットボトル, 古紙

meaning: Clean, empty, 100% plastic items under 30 cm: packaging and also plastic products like hangers or CDs. Clear or semi-clear bag. Not PET bottle bodies.
elsewhere: 資源プラスチック, プラ, 容器包装プラスチック (some wards take only packaging)

meaning: Batteries, spray cans, gas canisters, lighters, fluorescent tubes, mercury thermometers. Collected on non-burnable day, put out by 12:30, separate bags marked キケン.
elsewhere: 有害ごみ (yūgai), 危険ごみ (kiken), 有害・危険ごみ

meaning: Anything about 30 cm or larger on one side. Needs a booking and a paid sticker (処理券) from a konbini.
elsewhere: 粗大ごみ is the same almost everywhere

meaning: Snack boxes, wrapping paper, envelopes, tissue boxes. Recyclable, but in a separate bag. Not receipts, oily or smelly paper.
elsewhere: 雑がみ (zatsugami), ミックスペーパー
